query: Do statins help in primary prevention?

results.title: Efficacy and safety of more intensive lowering of LDL cholesterol: a meta-analysis of data from 170,000 participants in 26 randomised trials
results.abstract: In a meta-analysis of 26 randomised trials of statin therapy, each 1.0 mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol was associated with a 10% proportional reduction in all-cause mortality and a 20% reduction in coronary heart disease death. Benefit extended to participants at lower baseline cardiovascular risk.
results.takeaway: statin benefit on vascular events extends to lower-risk primary-prevention populations, not only secondary prevention

results.title: Effect of statins on primary prevention of cardiovascular events: an updated meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
results.abstract: Across primary-prevention randomised controlled trials, statin therapy reduced the risk of major cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in participants without established cardiovascular disease, with an absolute benefit proportional to baseline risk.
results.takeaway: in people without established cardiovascular disease, statins reduce major cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality, scaled to baseline risk

results.title: Cost-effectiveness of statins for primary prevention in low-risk adults
results.abstract: A health-economic modelling study found statin therapy for primary prevention to be cost-effective across most low-risk strata under contemporary generic pricing, with sensitivity to assumptions about adherence and disutility from daily medication.
results.takeaway: statins for low-risk primary prevention are generally cost-effective under generic pricing, though results are sensitive to adherence assumptions
